title: Mouse Without Borders Portable 1.1.0
summary: The new drag-and-drop file-transfer system is now stable: whole folders, per-file progress, queue controls, checked recovery, clearer previews, and compact settings. Version 1.1.0 promotes the RC14 application code with version and documentation updates.
changes: Copy files and whole folders directly into an Explorer folder or your chosen receiving folder, with immediate Preparing feedback.
Use one transfer window with individual progress, overall speed/ETA, pause/resume/retry/cancel, and up/down queue controls from either PC.
Keep existing destination files: name collisions create separate copies. Resume uses checked saved progress; cancelled partial data is cleaned up.
Show sharper file-type drag previews with clean transparency, up to three representative types and a total count. Right-click cancels a cross-PC drag.
Use compact, responsive settings with tooltip explanations, a multiline IP mapping editor, receiving-folder and automatic-closing preferences, and Installation controls.
Retain the installer update/relaunch fixes, plain tray icon, bounded diagnostics, and strictly manual GitHub update checking.
testing: RC14 passed 138 automated Windows checks with one existing skip. The owner reports good operation on real PCs; exhaustive hardware and network edge cases have not been claimed.
The stable EXE is rebuilt and retested by Windows CI, with an executable-version check and a SHA-256 checksum.
Update every connected PC to 1.1.0. Finish or cancel active transfers first; keep the adjacent preferences and recovery files when replacing the EXE.
Existing RC14 preferences and recovery data keep the same formats. Release notes and the current transfer guide are in docs/RELEASE_1.1.0.md and docs/FILE_TRANSFERS.md.
known_limitations: Normal interactive Windows desktops only; no service or protected UAC/sign-in-screen control. Published builds are Windows x64 and unsigned.
The new transfer controls and recovery apply to drag-and-drop. Clipboard file copy/paste retains its separate transport.
Full-speed transfers can still cause mouse lag on busy Wi-Fi. Offline peers can only synchronize cancellation and cleanup when reachable again.
Folder copies can partially complete. A failed child does not undo finished files; review and retry individual failures.
